# PROMueve Nexus — Reuma Export Known Legacy (F1.3B)

**Status:** `ACCEPTED_ENGINEERING_CHARACTERIZATION`
**Issue / WO:** #396 — `WO-NEXUS-F1.3B`, work unit WU-B
**Scope:** legacy Reuma export transport (497-column v2 TSV rows) generated by `modules/exportManager.js`
**Related tooling:** `tools/reuma_export_harness.mjs`, `tools/reuma_export_harness_check.mjs` (WU-A), `tools/reuma_export_acceptance_check.mjs` (WU-B, this oracle)

## Purpose

Separate **acceptance** (golden, authority-backed invariants) from
**characterization** (KNOWN_LEGACY / NON_GOLDEN observations) for the legacy
Reuma 497-column export transport, per Architecture Freeze §8. The oracle in
`tools/reuma_export_acceptance_check.mjs` asserts only the former and prints
the latter. This protects the legacy transport for the future strangler
without canonizing its defects: golden assertions lock the contract the
strangler must reproduce; KNOWN_LEGACY items are documented defects or risks
that must NOT be silently inherited.

## Oracle authority basis

- The oracle computes the 497 count ITSELF by splitting each TSV row on
  `'\t'`. The legacy in-band `validateExportRowLength` console.warn is NEVER a
  PASS source — it is characterization evidence only.
- Golden positions are derived from production constants and the
  production-exposed header arrays on `HubTools.export`:
  `FINAL_V2_EXPORT_COLUMN_COUNT=497`, `LEGACY_EXTENSION_HEADERS_221_321`,
  `COMMON_V2_HEADERS`, `LES_V2_HEADERS`, `SJOGREN_V2_HEADERS`,
  `APS_DAPSA_V2_HEADERS`. Block offsets: legacy base `[0..219]`, extension
  `[220..320]`, common `[321..364]` (321 = `HISTORICAL_EXPORT_COLUMN_COUNT`),
  then LES, Sjögren and APs/DAPSA blocks to 497.
- `LEGACY_BASE_COLUMN_COUNT=220` and `HISTORICAL_EXPORT_COLUMN_COUNT=321` are
  not exposed on `HubTools.export`; the oracle parses them read-only from
  `modules/exportManager.js` and fails closed if they or the block arithmetic
  change.
- Legacy base columns 1 (patientId), 5 (visit type) and 7 (pathology token)
  are set by explicit generator code in every base generator; the oracle
  asserts them with the derivation recorded, backed by the 220-column base
  block size.
- The oracle fails closed rather than passing on doubt: any position it
  cannot derive from the above authority is classified KNOWN_LEGACY, never
  faked as golden.

## ACCEPTANCE (golden, asserted by the oracle)

- **A1 exact length:** every one of the 10 supported journeys (AR/EspA/APs/
  LES/Sjögren × primera/seguimiento) produces exactly 497 fields, counted by
  the oracle itself.
- **A2 identity/visit:** each row carries its own patientId (field 1), the
  correct visit-type marker (field 5: `'Primera Visita'` / `'Seguimiento'`)
  and the correct pathology token (field 7), and no other journey's synthetic
  treatment marker appears in it.
- **A3 sentinel preservation at authority-derived positions:** numeric `0`
  rendered as `'0'` (not `''` / `'ND'`) at `Hemograma_Fecha_Solicitud`;
  explicit `'NA'` preserved verbatim at `ANA` and `Decision_Clinica_Manual`
  and at comorbilidad.hta (legacy column 115); explicit `'ND'` preserved
  verbatim at `ExtraAR_Anemia` and `Estado_Prebiologico_Final`; `''`
  preserved at `Hemograma_Observaciones` and `Observaciones_Prebiologico`;
  and false → `'NO'` rendered distinctly from missing → `'ND'` at
  `Decision_Clinica_Manual` and comorbilidad.hta (legacy column 115) across
  journeys.
- **A4 synthetic-only:** every patientId starts with `'SYN-'`; no documented
  real-format identifier shape (Spanish DNI/NIE patterns, intentionally
  minimal) appears in any row.

Planted negatives (in-memory only) prove each class can fail: N1 length
drift (496-field row → A1), N2 journey mix (swapped rows → A2), N3 value
collapse (sentinel `0` → `''` → A3), N4 contamination (foreign marker → A2),
N5 non-synthetic id (DNI-shaped id → A4).

## KNOWN_LEGACY / NON_GOLDEN (characterization, never asserted)

1. **Length enforcement is warn-only.** `validateExportRowLength` inside
   production only emits a `console.warn` when a row is not 497 columns; it
   returns `undefined`, never blocks, never fails. A drifted row still
   reaches the transport. The oracle's A1 is the independent guard.
2. **Legacy-base positions without exposed header arrays.** Column meanings
   set only by inline generator code are not asserted golden: hlaB27
   (column 9), dolorNocturno (column 106), extraArticular.digestiva
   (column 112), mdaCumple (column 193, AR base; also APs seguimiento).
   They are documented here instead of being faked.
3. **false-vs-missing collapse on legacy-base fallbacks.** dolorNocturno uses
   fallback `'NO'` and mdaCumple a `? 'SI' : 'NO'` ternary: explicit `false`
   and a missing key render identically. Demonstrated by the oracle's
   characterization case (removing the key leaves the row byte-identical).
4. **Raw `datos.X || ''` reads in the EspA/APs generators.** Fields such as
   hlaB27, peso or others read with `|| ''` would collapse numeric `0` and
   `false` to `''`. Verified read-only: on the frozen corpus no sentinel
   value flows through a raw `|| ''` read (the numeric 0 sentinel at
   `Hemograma_Fecha_Solicitud` is read via `getExportValue`, which skips only
   `undefined`/`null`/`''` so numeric 0 survives). This remains a latent risk
   for any future corpus that places 0/false in those fields.
5. **Empty string vs missing.** `getExportValue`/`getExportState` treat `''`
   like absent when a non-empty fallback exists; `''` is only preserved where
   the fallback is `''` (e.g. the observation columns asserted in A3).

## Boundary

None of the KNOWN_LEGACY items above is an acceptance criterion. The golden
section is the contract the future strangler implementation must reproduce;
the characterization section is the defect/risk inventory it must not
silently inherit. Production code is never modified by the harness, the
oracle or this check; all mutations used for falsification live in memory.
